commands.name: dev
commands.summary: Serve a deck with hot reload
commands.help:
Usage: deckster dev [deck] [--port <n>] [--host] [--brand <name>] [--mcp]
                [--agent claude|codex] [--agent-panel right|bottom] [--agent-model <m>]
                [--agent-web]

Serves a deck with hot reload. When several decks exist, open the printed chooser URL to pick one.
It runs until you press q or Ctrl+C.

Arguments:
  deck            Deck folder name under decks/. Defaults to $DECK, the sole deck, or the chooser.

Options:
  --port <n>      Use this port for the deck or chooser and fail if it is taken.
                  Default: the first free port from 5173.
  --host          Listen on all network interfaces, for example to present from a phone.
  --brand <name>  Render with brands/<name> instead of the deck config's brand.
  --mcp           Also serve the deck's MCP tools at /__deck/mcp on 127.0.0.1, for agents (Claude
                  Code, Codex). Requests need a per-run bearer token, which is written with the port
                  to .deck/agent/<deck>/server.json (mode 0600) until the server stops. Run
                  `deckster mcp <deck>` for ready-to-paste client configuration.
  --agent <name>  Add the agent chat beside the slide: claude or codex. It runs that
                  CLI with your own login, one process per prompt; every turn can be undone.
                  Implies --mcp. Check the set-up with `deckster agent doctor`.
                  The agent edits only the deck's content: slide files (.mdx, .tsx) in slides/ and media and data in assets/ and public/, in a working copy the editor copies into the deck; the slide list changes only through the deck tools, and anything else it writes is ignored.
                  See docs/agent.md.
  --agent-panel <right|bottom>
                  Where the chat docks. Default: right.
  --agent-model <name>
                  The model the agent uses. Default: the CLI's own default (for Codex, the model
                  in $CODEX_HOME/config.toml).
  --agent-web     Let the agent search the web and read pages (Claude's WebSearch and WebFetch
                  tools, Codex's live web search). Off by default: pages are text from outside
                  the repository that the agent reads while it edits code your browser runs, and
                  its queries and the addresses it opens leave this machine.
  -h, --help      Show this help.

commands.name: present
commands.summary: Open a deck in its own window, with displays and presenter view
commands.help:
Usage: deckster present [deck] [--brand <name>] [--port <n>] [--built] [--fullscreen]
                    [--display <n>] [--presenter [display]] [--kiosk] [--browser] [--verbose]
                    [--agent claude|codex] [--agent-panel right|bottom] [--agent-model <m>]
                    [--agent-web]
       deckster present --list-displays [--json]

Opens a deck in its own desktop window (Electron) and serves it with hot reload, so edits show at
once. With several decks and no name, choose a deck in the gallery. Use Back to decks to end the
current presentation and choose another. Quit Deckster or press Ctrl+C to end the command.
The terminal shows a short status (the
URL, the window, the agent and its turns); --verbose adds the dev server's log.

Arguments:
  deck            Deck folder name under decks/. Default: $DECK, then the only deck, then the gallery.

Options:
  --brand <name>  Render with brands/<name> instead of the deck config's brand.
  --port <n>      Set the deck or gallery port. Fail if it is taken. Default: first free port
                  from 5173 (4173 for a direct --built presentation).
  --built         Build the deck and present the static build instead of the dev server: no hot
                  reload, comments, agent or other dev tools. Cannot be combined with --brand or
                  --agent.
  --fullscreen    Make the audience window fullscreen.
  --display <n>   Open the audience window on display n (see --list-displays). Default: the
                  primary display, or the display that is not the presenter's.
  --presenter [n] Also open the presenter window, with notes and timer, on display n. Default: the
                  other display; with one display both windows share it. The audience window then
                  stays windowed.
  --kiosk         Fullscreen with no menu; Cmd/Ctrl+Q must be pressed twice to quit.
                  In the gallery, Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+B returns from the active presentation.
  --browser       Open the deck in Chrome's app mode (else the default browser) instead of
                  Electron, and print the URL. The fallback when Electron's binary is not
                  downloaded.
  --list-displays Print the connected displays and exit.
  --json          With --list-displays, print { ok, displays } as JSON.
  --verbose       Also print the dev server's log (hot updates, requests).
  --agent <name>  Add the agent chat beside the slide: claude or codex. It runs that
                  CLI with your own login, one process per prompt; every turn can be undone.
                  Implies --mcp. Check the set-up with `deckster agent doctor`.
                  The agent edits only the deck's content: slide files (.mdx, .tsx) in slides/ and media and data in assets/ and public/, in a working copy the editor copies into the deck; the slide list changes only through the deck tools, and anything else it writes is ignored.
                  See docs/agent.md.
  --agent-panel <right|bottom>
                  Where the chat docks. Default: right.
  --agent-model <name>
                  The model the agent uses. Default: the CLI's own default (for Codex, the model
                  in $CODEX_HOME/config.toml).
  --agent-web     Let the agent search the web and read pages (Claude's WebSearch and WebFetch
                  tools, Codex's live web search). Off by default: pages are text from outside
                  the repository that the agent reads while it edits code your browser runs, and
                  its queries and the addresses it opens leave this machine.
                  In the window, only the window's own first page load gets the session that
                  the agent panel and comments need.
  -h, --help      Show this help.

Electron's binary is downloaded once with `deckster electron install` (about 120 MB). See docs/present.md.

commands.name: electron
commands.summary: Download, update or check the Electron binary deckster present uses
commands.help:
Usage: deckster electron install [--force] [--json]
       deckster electron update [--json]
       deckster electron status [--json]

Manages the Electron binary `deckster present` opens its windows with (about 120 MB). npm, pnpm and
yarn often skip the download when they install @deckster/cli, so run `deckster electron install`
once after installing. Nothing else needs Electron: every other command, and
`deckster present --browser`, use Chrome.

Commands:
  install   Downloads the Electron version this CLI was built with, unless it is already there.
            It runs Electron's own downloader, which checks the published checksums and reuses
            Electron's download cache. It honours HTTPS_PROXY and ELECTRON_MIRROR.
  update    Downloads Electron again when the binary on disk is not the version this CLI needs,
            as after upgrading @deckster/cli. The version comes with the CLI: to move to a newer
            Electron, upgrade @deckster/cli first.
  status    Prints whether the binary is downloaded, its version and where it is.

Options:
  --force   With install: remove the binary and download it again, skipping the cache.
  --json    Print { ok, downloaded, electron: { directory, version, downloadedVersion,
            executable, ready } }. A failure prints { ok: false, error: { type, message } }.
  -h, --help  Show this help.

Exits with 1 when the download fails, or when status finds no usable binary.

commands.name: build
commands.summary: Build a deck (or every deck) to decks/<deck>/dist
commands.help:
Usage: deckster build [deck] [--with-exports] [--all] [--out <dir>] [--include-scratch]

Builds a deck to decks/<deck>/dist as static files that can be hosted under any path.

With --out, builds decks into one site folder instead: <dir>/<deck>/ for each deck, with a
thumbnail.png of its first slide, and <dir>/index.html, a gallery of the decks (title, brand,
slide count, thumbnail, links to each deck and to its PDF and PPTX). Everything is relative, so
the folder can be hosted under any path. The entire destination folder is replaced with the
selected decks and their gallery. The site leaves out scratch decks, whose folder name
starts with zz- (throwaway decks such as trial runs), unless --include-scratch is given or the deck is named.

Arguments:
  deck          Deck folder name under decks/. Default: $DECK, else every deck.

Options:
  --all           Build every deck, ignoring $DECK. Cannot be combined with a deck name.
  --out <dir>     Write a site folder (see above) instead of decks/<deck>/dist only. The
                  per-deck builds are still written to decks/<deck>/dist first.
  --include-scratch
                  With --out, also build zz- decks into the site. Without --out every deck,
                  zz- ones included, is built already.
  --with-exports  Also export the deck to <deck>.pdf and <deck>.pptx beside index.html, so a
                  <Download file="<deck>.pdf"> button on a slide can link to them; with --out
                  the gallery links to them.
  -h, --help      Show this help.

commands.name: preview
commands.summary: Serve the built output of a deck
commands.help:
Usage: deckster preview [deck] [--port <n>] [--host]

Serves the built output of a deck from decks/<deck>/dist until you press Ctrl+C. Run
`deckster build <deck>` first.

Arguments:
  deck          Deck folder name under decks/. Default: $DECK, else "hello".

Options:
  --port <n>    Use this port and fail if it is taken.
  --host        Listen on all network interfaces.
  -h, --help    Show this help.

commands.name: shot
commands.summary: Write PNG screenshots of slides (and steps)
commands.help:
Usage: deckster shot <deck> [slide] [--steps] [--brand <name>] [--out <dir>] [--scale <n>] [--json]

Renders a deck in static mode and writes a 1920x1080 PNG per slide, so you can look at the
slides, hidden ones included. Open the files to inspect them; --json lists them for scripts. A
slide that throws is still captured, showing its error, and the command exits with 1.

Arguments:
  deck            Deck folder name under decks/.
  slide           One slide, by id or 1-based number. Default: every slide, hidden ones too.

Options:
  --steps         One PNG per step instead of one per slide, named NN-id.stepK.png (K from 0).
                  Without it each slide is captured at its last step, with everything shown.
  --brand <name>  Render with brands/<name> instead of the deck config's brand.
  --out <dir>     Output folder. Default: .deck/shots/<deck>, or
                  .deck/shots/<deck>@<brand> with --brand.
  --scale <n>     Pixel density from 0.25 to 4; 2 writes 3840x2160 images. Default: 1.
  --json          Print { deck, brand, outDir, ok, files: [{ path, slide, number, step, hidden,
                  width, height, error }], pageErrors }. hidden is true for a slide with
                  `hidden: true`. error is what a broken slide threw, else null; pageErrors
                  are errors thrown while the deck loaded. A failure prints
                  { ok: false, error: { type, message } } instead.
  -h, --help      Show this help.

Files are named 03-request-flow.png and 03-request-flow.step2.png. A run over the whole deck
removes older screenshots with that naming from the output folder first.

commands.name: diff
commands.summary: Show which slides changed visually against a git ref or baseline
commands.help:
Usage: deckster diff <deck> [--base <ref|dir>] [--brand <name>] [--steps] [--threshold <n>]
                 [--out <dir>] [--fail-on-change] [--json]
       deckster diff <deck> --save-baseline [dir] [--brand <name>] [--steps] [--json]

Shows which slides of a deck changed visually, for pull requests and for agents checking their
own edits. It renders the deck now and at the base, matches slides by id (so a reordered deck
reports "moved", not a change in every slide) and compares them pixel by pixel.

Statuses: unchanged, changed, added, removed, moved (same pictures, another place in the order).

Arguments:
  deck            Deck folder name under decks/.

Options:
  --base <x>      What to compare against. A folder of PNGs made by `deckster shot` (same names), else
                  a git ref. Default: HEAD in a git repository; outside one, the folder
                  --save-baseline writes. A ref is extracted with `git archive` into a temporary
                  folder that borrows this workspace's node_modules by link, so nothing is installed
                  and the repository is untouched; the folder is deleted afterwards. The ref is
                  rendered with its own packages (engine, kit, brands and Vite plugin), so a change
                  to a layout shows up too.
  --brand <name>  Render both with brands/<name> instead of the deck config's brand. The default
                  folders get an @<name> suffix.
  --steps         Compare every step, not only each slide's finished state. A baseline folder
                  must then hold step pictures (`deckster shot <deck> --steps`).
  --threshold <n> A picture counts as changed when more than this share of its pixels changed
                  visibly, from 0 to 1. Default: 0.
  --out <dir>     Report folder. Default: .deck/diff/<deck>[@<brand>].
  --fail-on-change  Exit with 1 when any slide changed, was added, removed or moved.
  --save-baseline [dir]
                  Instead of comparing, render the deck into a baseline folder (default
                  .deck/baseline/<deck>[@<brand>]) to compare against later. This is the
                  way to use `deckster diff` without git.
  --json          Print the report: { ok, deck, brand, base, baseKind, steps, threshold, outDir,
                  counts, slides: [{ id, status, beforeNumber, afterNumber, moved,
                  differenceRatio, before, after, compare, steps? }] } with absolute picture
                  paths; steps are { step, status, differenceRatio, before, after, compare }.
                  Pictures exist only for slides and steps that differ; the other paths are null.
                  --save-baseline prints { ok, deck, brand, baseline, files }. A failure prints
                  { ok: false, error: { type, message } } instead.
  -h, --help      Show this help.

The report folder holds index.html (open it to see the changes), summary.md (a table for a pull
request comment, with relative picture links), report.json (the same as --json, with paths
relative to the folder) and the folders before/, after/ and compare/ with the pictures of what
differs. Exit code: 0 unless the command fails, or --fail-on-change finds a change.

commands.name: export
commands.summary: Export a deck to PDF, PNG and PowerPoint
commands.help:
Usage: deckster export <deck> [--pdf] [--png] [--pptx] [options]

Exports a deck rendered in static mode. Without a format flag it writes the PDF and the PPTX.

Formats:
  --pdf             One page per slide at its last step: Chromium's vector PDF, the 1920x1080
                    canvas on 1440x810 pt pages (20x11.25 in), fonts embedded, external and
                    slide-to-slide links, a bookmark and page label per slide, tagged for screen
                    readers, the deck title and the brand's language. Videos, iframes and apps
                    show their posters.
  --png             PNG screenshots, as `deckster shot` writes them, in <out>/png.
  --pptx            PowerPoint: a theme and slide master per brand surface in use with the brand's
                    chrome and a slide number, the deck's layouts with placeholders placed and
                    styled as the deck sets them, editable text that wraps where the web wraps, the
                    brand's fonts embedded as static instances, shapes, gradients, pictures (JPEG
                    when opaque, each stored once), tables, charts and diagrams, speaker notes,
                    links and step animations; what PowerPoint cannot draw is a picture.

Options:
  --steps           One page or slide per step instead of one per slide.
  --slides <list>   Slides to export, such as 3,5-9 or cover,heat-map. Default: every slide that is
                    not hidden. A hidden slide you name here is exported: as an
                    ordinary page in the PDF and a PNG, still marked hidden in the PPTX.
  --include-hidden  Export hidden slides too (`hidden: true` in the frontmatter): as ordinary PDF
                    pages and PNGs, and as hidden slides in the PPTX (PowerPoint skips them in a
                    slide show). Without it they are left out and the summary says how many.
  --brand <name>    Render with brands/<name> instead of the deck config's brand.
  --out <path>      Output folder, or a .pdf or .pptx file when exporting that one format.
                    Default: .deck/exports/<deck> (or <deck>@<brand>).
  --notes           Add speaker notes pages (slide plus notes) after the slides in the PDF.
  --scale <n>       Pixel density of PNGs and of the PPTX's pictures, from 0.25 to 4.
                    Default: 1 for PNGs; 2 for PPTX pictures, at most 1920x1080 pixels each.
  --mode <mode>     PPTX mode: hybrid (native where faithful, a picture where not; default),
                    native (never a picture; reports what it dropped) or image (one picture per
                    slide with notes and link hotspots).
  --outline-text    Draw display-size text (60px and up: titles, statements, stats) as vector
                    shapes in the brand font at its exact axes, so it looks the same without the
                    font installed; the text stays in the title placeholder for outline view.
  --no-embed-fonts  Do not embed the brand's fonts in the PPTX; text names the brand's families,
                    with PANOSE and pitch so apps substitute a similar font.
  --fonts <set>     brand (default) or system: render and measure the deck in each family's
                    substitute (Arial, Georgia, Courier New...) so line breaks are right in apps
                    without the brand's fonts, such as Keynote or Google Slides.
  --no-animations   Do not turn step reveals into PowerPoint click animations.
  --no-embed-media  Keep videos as posters instead of embedding MP4 and MOV files.
  --max-media-mb <n> The largest video to embed. Default: 50.
  --dry-run         List per slide what the PPTX draws natively and what it rasterises, and why;
                    writes nothing.
  --verify          Export the PPTX, validate it with the Open XML SDK (Docker), render it back to
                    pictures and compare each text block, chart, diagram, picture and table with the
                    web slide: where it landed, its size and its line count. Prints the worst
                    regions per slide and writes side-by-side pictures, crops of the regions that
                    differ and report.json to <out>/verify.
  --strict          With --verify, exit non-zero when any region differs or nothing was rendered.
  --renderer <ids>  Renderers for --verify, comma-separated: libreoffice (Docker, the export's
                    fonts installed), libreoffice-nofonts (Docker, no brand fonts and embedded
                    fonts removed: the substitutes), libreoffice-embedded (Docker, no brand fonts,
                    the file's embedded fonts), quicklook (macOS), keynote (macOS; opens Keynote,
                    needs Automation permission). Default: libreoffice,libreoffice-nofonts,quicklook.
  --json            Print the result as JSON.
  -h, --help        Show this help.

commands.name: lint
commands.summary: Check a deck for schema errors, overflow, contrast and off-brand values
commands.help:
Usage: deckster lint <deck> [--brand <name>] [--json]

Checks a deck and exits non-zero when it finds errors.

  1. Schema: the deck config, the brand and every slide file go through the same checks as
     `deckster build`, and each problem is reported with the file and its fix. When files fail, the
     rendered checks are skipped, because the deck cannot render.
  2. Rendered: the deck is opened in static mode and every step of every slide is measured.
  3. Deck: rules over the whole deck, such as the order of layouts.

Rules (the minimum text size is 20px on the 1920x1080 canvas, from @deckster/brand):
  schema              Deck config, brand, frontmatter and MDX problems from the build pipeline.
  render-error                A slide threw while rendering, or the page threw an uncaught error. (error)
  canvas-overflow             Content extends past the edge of the 1920x1080 canvas and is clipped. (error)
  container-overflow          Content is larger than its own container and is clipped or spills out of it. (error)
  text-truncated              Text is cut short with an ellipsis or a line clamp, so part of it is not shown. (error)
  text-overlap                Two pieces of text are drawn over each other. (error)
  min-font-size               Text appears below the minimum type size (after transforms and SVG scaling) on the canvas. (error)
  contrast                    Text contrast against its background is below WCAG AA (4.5:1, or 3:1 for large text). (error)
  off-brand                   Colors, font families, type sizes or Tailwind numeric spacing that are not brand tokens. (error)
  low-res-image               A raster image has fewer pixels than the size it is drawn at on the 1x canvas. (warning)
  table-too-dense             A table does not fit its slide even at the smallest type the brand allows, so it must lose rows or columns. (error)
  app-missing-poster          An <AppFrame> has no poster to show in static mode, export and offline. (error)
  app-missing                 An <AppFrame app> names an app the deck does not have. (error)
  app-external-src            An <AppFrame src> loads an external page and has no recorded fallback video. (warning)
  video-cue-posters           A cued <Video> has no poster per part, so its steps export as the same still. (warning)
  export-missing-poster       Live media without a poster exports as a stray frame, a picture or nothing. (warning)
  chart-empty                 A chart draws no marks, or a line or area chart has a single point. (error)
  chart-truncated-axis        A bar chart sets `min` above zero without `truncate`, so its bars would lie. (error)
  chart-too-many-series       A chart draws more series in their own color than the brand's categorical palette has colors. (warning)
  chart-too-many-categories   A chart draws more bars, stages, rows or items than reads at a glance on a slide. (warning)
  chart-pie-slices            A <Donut> has more than 5 slices. (warning)
  chart-no-highlight          A chart with several series or many categories highlights nothing. (warning)
  chart-topic-title           A chart slide's title looks like a topic ("X by Y", "X vs Y", a short noun phrase), not a takeaway. (warning)
  chart-missing-unit          A chart's values have no unit and no caption naming the measure. (warning)
  chart-legend-avoidable      A chart shows a legend where direct labels would name the series. (warning)
  chart-funnel-grows          A <Funnel> has a stage that holds more than the stage before it. (warning)
  broken-image                An image failed to load, so the slide shows a broken image or nothing. (error)
  diagram-too-dense           A diagram shows more than 12 nodes or 16 edges at once, or its nodes are packed tighter than its gutters. (warning)
  diagram-label-overlap       A diagram edge label covers a node, a group label or another edge label. (warning)
  diagram-unlabeled-edge      A diagram edge without a label is ambiguous: it doubles another edge, or its siblings are labeled. (warning)
  diagram-small-text          Text in a diagram appears smaller than the brand's caption and label steps. (warning)
  diagram-overlap             A diagram draws nodes, groups or group labels on top of each other. (error)
  diagram-edge-overlap        Two diagram edges that share no node run along one line and read as one. (warning)
  diagram-badge-overlap       A diagram badge sits on an edge or its arrowhead. (warning)
  diagram-long-word           A diagram breaks a word inside a node title or edge label, or cuts a label short, because it is too long to fit. (warning)
  diagram-card-missing        A diagram part names a card the brand does not have, so it uses another card. (warning)
  content-budget              A layout slot holds more words, bullets or lines of code than the layout's budget. (error)
  slot-content                A slot holds content its layout's contract does not accept: a list where it takes no bullets, another kind than it lists, or more than the one table, chart or image it is for. (error)
  missing-notes               A slide has no speaker notes. (warning)
  layout-repetition           3 or more slides in a row use the same layout on the same surface, counting shown slides only. (warning)
  brand-layout-fallback       A slide names a layout that only another brand defines, so it renders with that layout's kit fallback. (warning)
  few-builds                  Fewer than 25% of a deck's chart, diagram and code slides (4 or more) build in steps; hidden slides are left out. (warning)
  time-budget                 The slides' budgets add up to more than the talk's duration (the deck config's `duration`); hidden slides are left out. (error)
  open-comments               A slide has open review comments in .feedback/. (warning)

Mark decoration with aria-hidden="true" or data-decorative: the overflow and text rules skip it.

Options:
  --brand <name>  Lint the deck rendered with brands/<name> instead of the deck config's brand.
  --json          Print { deck, brand, ok, summary: { errors, warnings, slides, steps,
                  budgetSeconds }, findings } as JSON. Each finding has slide, file, step, rule,
                  severity, message, fix and selector. A failure (bad arguments, unknown deck,
                  browser problems) prints { ok: false, error: { type, message } } instead.
  -h, --help      Show this help.

commands.name: layouts
commands.summary: List the layouts available to a deck
commands.help:
Usage: deckster layouts [deck] [--brand <name>] [--summary] [--json]

Lists the layouts a slide can name in its `layout:` frontmatter: the engine's and the kit's, and
the ones the deck's brand brings in brands/<name>/layouts.ts (source "brand:<name>"). A brand's
layouts are the template the organisation expects, so prefer them when one fits; slides on a brand
layout fall back to its kit layout when the deck moves to a brand without it.

Arguments:
  deck          Deck folder name under decks/. Default: $DECK, else "hello", else the only deck.

Options:
  --brand <name>
                List the layouts of this brand instead of the deck config's, as `deckster dev
                --brand` renders it. A brand that does not load leaves its own layouts out, with
                a warning on stderr (and in "warnings" with --json).
  --summary     One compact entry per layout, for a first look: name, the first sentence of its
                description, default surface, title limit, slots (`*` required) with what each
                accepts and its budget, and item lists with their counts (stats[2-4]). With
                --json, { deck, warnings, layouts: [{ name, description, surface, titleMaxChars, slots:
                { <slot>: { accepts, required, maxWords?, maxBullets?, maxLines? } }, items:
                [{ field, min, max }] }] }. The brand's layouts come first, under a heading that
                names the brand, and each also has source ("brand:<name>") and fallback. Without
                --summary the output is the full catalog.
  --json        Print { deck, slideFrontmatter, warnings, layouts }. slideFrontmatter is the JSON Schema of
                the fields every slide takes. Each layout has name, source (a package, or
                "brand:<name>" for a brand layout), fallback (the kit layout a brand layout falls
                back to, else null), label (a brand layout's name in its source template, else
                null), description,
                frontmatter (JSON Schema of its own fields, with defaults), fields ({ required,
                default, allowed, hint } by name), title ({ required, maxChars } or null),
                surface (the default surface or null), slots ({ tag, description, required,
                accepts } by name; body is the content outside slot tags), budget (maxWords
                and maxBullets per slot, maxLines for code; the same in every brand), variants
                ([{ name, when: { fields, counts, filled }, budget, fields, limits }]: budget and
                fields are what the variant tightens, limits { budget, fields } every limit a
                slide that matches it is held to, field limits by path such as stats[].label),
                example ({ frontmatter, body, mdx }) and pptx.
  -h, --help    Show this help.

commands.name: icons
commands.summary: List the icon names every brand has
commands.help:
Usage: deckster icons [--brand <a,b>] [--search <text>] [--json]

Lists the icon names a deck can use in every brand it renders in. Each brand draws icons from one
Iconify set (its `icons.set`); a name works in all of those brands only when every set has it.
Use these names in <Icon name="...">, in a layout's `icon` field and for a diagram node's `icon`.

Options:
  --brand <a,b>    The brands to share names between, comma-separated brand folder names.
                   Default: every brand in brands/.
  --search <text>  Only names that contain the text, such as `--search arrow`.
  --json           Print { brands: [{ name, set }], count, icons: [...] }: every shared name
                   (narrowed by --search), where count is how many there are.
  -h, --help       Show this help.

Plain output prints the count and the first 120 names; narrow it with --search or
print them all with --json.

commands.name: charts
commands.summary: List the chart and number components and when to use each
commands.help:
Usage: deckster charts [--json]

Lists the chart and number components a slide can use, each with the messages it is the right
form for. Start from the message (what you are saying), then pick the form.

Options:
  --json        Print { shared, types, charts, messages, insight, spec }. shared describes
                the props several charts take once ({ type, required, default, description }
                by name). Each chart has name, kind, useWhen, messages (from: single number,
                comparison, ranking, trend, change between two points, part-to-whole,
                distribution, correlation, flow, exact values), avoid, data (the shape of its
                rows), nulls (how it draws a missing value), shared (the names of the shared
                props it takes), props (its own props, by name), limits (the numbers deckster lint
                holds it to), example (MDX), accessibility and native (the PowerPoint chart
                PPTX export builds, or null). A prop name in neither shared nor props throws.
                types lists the fields of RowStat, ProgressItem, TableColumn, SeriesInput,
                FormatOptions, Highlight and each Annotation. messages lists the components
                for each message, in catalog order (not ranked: read each one's useWhen
                and avoid to choose); insight explains the props, highlight,
                annotations, labels, axis honesty, steps, data, nulls, format, relative and
                limits; spec names the attribute and module of each figure's serialisable
                description.
  -h, --help    Show this help.

commands.name: diagrams
commands.summary: List the diagram components, node kinds, cards and animation primitives
commands.help:
Usage: deckster diagrams [--json]

Lists the diagram components a slide can use and the parts inside them, with every prop, the node
kinds, the edge options, the cards and the animation primitives (packets, journeys, state changes,
focus), each with when to use it and an example, plus the limits deckster lint holds diagrams to and
how to write diagrams in TSX. The cards listed are the five every brand has; `deckster brand <name>`
lists a brand's own.

Options:
  --json        Print { shared, components, nodeKinds, edgeOptions, edgeFlow, cards, animation,
                states, stateSynonyms, packetRoles, svgRoles, limits, longText, tsx, notes }. shared
                describes the props several components take once ({ type, required, default,
                description, values } by name), and longText says once what happens to long node
                titles, subtitles and edge labels. Each component has name (the tag, as in deck
                charts and deckster components: "Flow"), role (diagram or part), inside (where a part
                goes), useWhen, example (MDX), shared (the names of the shared props it takes),
                props (its own props, by name), children, limits and, only where it has its own
                rule, longText. A prop name in neither shared nor props, or a value outside its
                values, fails the build naming the closest one.
                Each node kind has kind, aliases, shape, icons (the icon name by icon set, or
                null) and useWhen; edgeOptions and animation are lists of { name, useWhen,
                example }; edgeFlow describes the fields of <Edge flow={{ ... }}>; cards has
                resolution (how a node picks its card), standard (the five cards every brand has,
                by name, with their look), custom (where a brand's own cards are listed: deck
                brand <name>) and rules (what a card does not change); limits are the
                node, edge, column, row and text-wrap numbers; tsx has the import line, how icons
                and errors work, and an example slide.
  -h, --help    Show this help.

commands.name: components
commands.summary: List the code, media, link and demo components with their props
commands.help:
Usage: deckster components [--json]

Lists the MDX components a slide can use besides charts (deckster charts) and diagrams (deck
diagrams): code, terminals, media, icons, links, live demos, steps and notes.

Options:
  --json        Print { shared, components, insight }, shaped like deckster charts and deck
                diagrams: shared is empty (no props are shared between these components). Each
                component has name (the tag, such as "Code"), kind (code, media, icon, link,
                app, motion or notes), useWhen, avoid, shared (always []), props (by name:
                { type, required, default, description }) and example (MDX). A prop name a component
                does not list is refused with the closest one, at build time in MDX and when
                the slide renders in TSX, and so is a missing required prop. insight explains
                props, files, static mode, steps and the build warnings deckster lint reports.
  -h, --help    Show this help.

commands.name: brand
commands.summary: Print a brand's resolved tokens, check a brand, or add one from git
commands.help:
Usage: deckster brand [name] [--json]
       deckster brand check <name> [--json]
       deckster brand add <source> [--force] [--json]

Prints a brand's resolved tokens, validates a brand without rendering a deck, or adds a brand
from a git repository.

  deckster brand [name]        A summary of brands/<name>: families, type scale, spacing, each
                           surface's roles, with the small-text color of a role that reaches only
                           3:1, the diagram look (edges, groups, labels, geometry, text and kind
                           mappings) and every diagram card with its colors on the default
                           surface. Default: "default". With --json, every resolved token:
                           palette, surfaces (roles, text colors, backdrop, background layers,
                           code, diagram, diagramCards, data with the chart plate, charts,
                           shadows), gradients, typography, shape, spacing, logo, chrome, motion,
                           data, charts and diagram. diagram includes align, edges, groups, labels,
                           nodes, notes, kinds and cards. Cards gives geometry and typography
                           by name, the five standard cards first, with titleOwn (the brand wrote
                           the title type, on the card or its default card); a surface's
                           diagramCards holds each card's colors and shadow there, after any
                           recoloring the surface writes, with nodeFill (the fill is that
                           surface's diagram node color). Colors are hex, sizes canvas px.
                           It also prints the number and names of the brand's own layouts
                           (brands/<name>/layouts.ts). With --json, layouts has each
                           layout with its defaults filled in.
  deckster brand check <name>  Loads and validates brands/<name> and prints every error and warning
                           with its field and fix. This includes its layouts: each must name a
                           kit or engine layout as its fallback, bind only slots and fields that
                           layout has, bind every one it requires, and not clash with a kit
                           layout's name. Exits with 1 when it has errors.
  deckster brand add <source>  Copies a brand folder from a git repository into brands/<name>, named
                           by the brand's `name`. <source> is gh:owner/repo/<folder>#<ref>
                           (over https), a GitHub link (https://github.com/owner/repo/tree/<ref>/
                           <folder>), or any https or ssh address with the folder after //, such
                           as git@github.com:owner/repo.git//brands/acme#v2. Without #<ref>, the
                           default branch. It runs your git, so your credential helper, SSH key
                           and url.<base>.insteadOf rules apply. brand.ts and layouts.ts are read
                           as data and never run; the brand is checked before anything is
                           written, and only brand.ts, layouts.ts, images, fonts and documents
                           are copied (no other code, symlinks or package files). Fonts are not
                           installed: it prints the commands to run next (pnpm install in this
                           repository, or npm install for missing fonts), then deckster brand check,
                           which checks what needs the fonts. Each git step that uses the
                           network may take up to 2 minutes.

Options:
  --json        For check: { brand, file, ok, errors, warnings }, each problem { path, message,
                fix }. For add: { ok, brand, dir, source, commit, replaced, files, written,
                skipped: [{ path, reason }], fonts: [{ name, version, installed }], warnings,
                next }. A failure prints { ok: false, error: { type, message } }.
  --force       For add: replace a brand of the same name the workspace already has.
  -h, --help    Show this help.

commands.name: new
commands.summary: Create a deck, or add a slide to one
commands.help:
Usage: deckster new <deck> [--title <text>] [--brand <name>] [--duration <length>]
       deckster new slide <deck> <id> [--layout <name>]
       deckster new app <deck> <name>

Scaffolds a deck, adds a slide to one, or adds a mini app to one.

  deckster new <deck>             Creates decks/<deck>/ with deck.config.ts (title, brand,
                              optional duration), and a first slide
                              that uses the title layout, from that layout's example. It passes
                              `deckster lint` as created.
  deckster new slide <deck> <id>  Creates slides/<id>.mdx from the layout's example (see
                              `deckster layouts --json`) with the slide's own title, and
                              appends <id> to the slide list in deck.config.ts.
  deckster new app <deck> <name>  Creates apps/<name>/ (index.html, main.tsx, app.tsx, app.css,
                              error-boundary.tsx), a React mini app wired to
                              @deckster/app-bridge, and prepares the deck
                              to build it. Show it with <AppFrame app="<name>" poster="..." />.
                              The deck builds it as an extra entry served at apps/<name>/.

Names are kebab-case: lowercase words joined by hyphens.

Options:
  --title <text>    The deck title for `deckster new <deck>`. Default: the name as a sentence. At most
                    as long as the title layout allows (the error says how many characters).
  --brand <name>    The brand folder under brands/ the deck uses, written to deck.config.ts.
                    Default: default.
  --duration <len>  The talk length, such as 20m, 90s or 1m30s, written to deck.config.ts as
                    `duration` (the presenter's pacing and the time-budget lint rule).
  --layout <name>   The layout for the new slide, from the layout catalog. Run
                    `deckster layouts` to list them. Default: default.
  -h, --help        Show this help.

commands.name: types
commands.summary: Write tsconfig.json so editors and tsc resolve @deckster imports
commands.help:
Usage: deckster types

Makes the workspace type-check in your editor and with `tsc`, without installing anything in it.
It writes tsconfig.json at the workspace root, and .deck/env.d.ts beside it:
  - `@deckster/*` imports map to the framework's source files in this install;
  - every other package a deck or brand imports (effect, react) resolves from the framework's own
    dependencies;
  - `*.mdx`, Node, Vite client and icon declarations are included.
Settings you already have in tsconfig.json are kept; only the paths `deckster types` manages are
replaced: `@deckster/*`, `effect`, `react` and `react-dom` (with their subpaths), and `*`. A
tsconfig.json that `extends` another keeps its own compiler options. A tsconfig.json with
comments, or one that is a symbolic link, is left alone: remove the comments or replace the link.

The paths name this install's folders. Run `deckster types` again after upgrading @deckster/cli, and
do not commit the result to a repository others install differently.

In the framework's own repository the packages are linked by the workspace and this does nothing.

Options:
  -h, --help  Show this help.

commands.name: comments
commands.summary: List, resolve, reopen, add and prune review comments
commands.help:
Usage: deckster comments <deck> [--open | --resolved | --all] [--slide <id>] [--json]
       deckster comments resolve <deck> <id> [--note <text>] [--json]
       deckster comments reopen <deck> <id> [--json]
       deckster comments add <deck> <slide> --text <text> [--line <n>] [--step <n>] [--type <type>]
                         [--json]
       deckster comments prune <deck> [--json]

Review comments on a deck: left in the browser in comment mode (press c in `deckster dev`) or
by agents, stored in decks/<deck>/.feedback/<slide-id>.json and committed with the deck. Each
comment names the file, line and column to edit, so it can be fixed without the browser.

  deckster comments <deck>          Lists open comments with file:line:column, anchor status, text and
                                screenshot (--resolved or --all for the others).
  resolve <deck> <id>           Marks a comment resolved, signed with $DECK_AUTHOR, else git's
                                user.name; --note says what changed. An already resolved
                                comment keeps its note.
  reopen <deck> <id>            Opens a resolved comment again; an open one is left as it is.
  add <deck> <slide>            Adds a comment on a slide, or with --line on that line of the slide
                                file, so agents can leave comments too.
  prune <deck>                  Removes the comments of slides the deck config does not list.

Anchor status: ok (the line still reads as it did), moved (found elsewhere: line is the new
place), guessed (the line was reworded: line is the nearby line most like it; check it), lost
(nothing matches: line is null and location names only the file; read the excerpt around
anchor.originalLine and the screenshot), none (a comment on a whole slide).

box and region are in canvas pixels of the 1920x1080 slide (origin top left), not screen pixels;
the JSON says so in units.

Options:
  --open, --resolved, --all  Which comments to list. Default: --open.
  --slide <id>      Only this slide's comments; an id the deck does not have is a usage error
                    naming its slides.
  --note <text>     What changed, for resolve.
  --text <text>     The comment, for add.
  --line <n>        The line of the slide file the comment is about, for add.
  --step <n>        The step the comment is about, for add. Default: 0.
  --type <type>     fix, question or idea, for add.
  --json            Print JSON. The list is { deck, deckDir, counts: { open, resolved },
                    units: { box: "canvas-px", canvasWidth, canvasHeight }, comments }, each
                    comment with id, number, slide, slideNumber, step, status, type, target,
                    text, author, createdAt, updatedAt, location (file:line:column to edit; just
                    the file when line is null), file, line, column, anchor { status (ok, moved,
                    guessed, lost, none), originalLine, stamp, element
                    { tag, text, cssPath } }, excerpt { startLine, lines }, screenshot, box,
                    region, resolution { note, by, at } and hash. resolve, reopen and add print
                    { ok: true, changed, comment }, where changed is false when the comment was
                    already resolved (resolve) or open (reopen) and nothing was written; prune
                    prints { deck, removed: [{ slide, comments }] }.
                    A failure prints { ok: false, error: { type, message } }.
  -h, --help        Show this help.

commands.name: mcp
commands.summary: Print Claude Code and Codex configuration for a running deckster dev --mcp
commands.help:
Usage: deckster mcp [deck] [--json]

Prints ready-to-paste configuration that connects Claude Code and Codex to the MCP tools of a
running `deckster dev <deck> --mcp`: the environment variable that holds the token, a `.mcp.json`
snippet and the `claude mcp add` command, and a `config.toml` section and the `codex mcp add`
command. The port and token are read from .deck/agent/<deck>/server.json, which the dev server
writes while it runs. Without a running server it says how to start one.

Arguments:
  deck          Deck folder name under decks/. Default: $DECK, else "hello".

Options:
  --json        Print { deck, url, tokenEnvVar, token, env, claude: { mcpJson, add }, codex:
                { configToml, add } }. A failure prints { ok: false, error: { type, message } }.
  -h, --help    Show this help.

commands.name: agent
commands.summary: Check the agent CLIs (Claude Code, Codex): installed, version, signed in
commands.help:
Usage: deckster agent doctor [--agent claude|codex] [--json]

Checks the agent CLIs `deckster dev --agent` and `deckster present --agent` drive: whether each binary is
on the PATH, its version (and whether it is the version the adapter was tested with), and whether
it is signed in, with the command that fixes each problem. It runs `claude --version`,
`claude auth status --json`, `codex --version` and `codex login status`; it never prints an
e-mail address or a token.

The agent edits only the deck's content: slide files (.mdx, .tsx) in slides/ and media and data in assets/ and public/, in a working copy the editor copies into the deck; the slide list changes only through the deck tools, and anything else it writes is ignored.

Options:
  --agent <name>  Check one provider: claude or codex. Default: both.
  --json          Print { ok, providers: [{ provider, label, installed, version, testedVersion,
                  signedIn, account, problem: { kind, message, fix } | null, warnings }] }. A
                  failure prints { ok: false, error: { type, message } }.
  -h, --help      Show this help.

Exits with 1 when a checked provider has a problem.
